title: Dispatch: olc5.12.3 + xt6m grant bind credits and single-use stacks (attempt 1, Sonnet)
description:
Implements eshyra-olc5.12.3 (non-anchored grants bind without their spend) and the stacking half of eshyra-xt6m. Read `bd show eshyra-olc5.12.3` and `bd show eshyra-xt6m`. Also read eshyra-olc5.12's notes, in particular the DESIGN RECONCILIATION of 2026-10-17, the olc5.12.13 consumption receipt, and the retired-id rule. They are merged on main (PR #665) and remain binding. Locate code by symbol name.

PROBLEM: in the pack, a grant whose cooldownEconomy is NOT grant-ended-anchored binds through start_effect with no spend at all (grantCooldownAnchoredTo is false). The affected grants are bag-of-tricks (uses, per-day), bowl/brazier/censer/stone elementals (uses, per-day), deck-of-illusions (cards, doses), figurine goat-of-traveling (hour charges), horn-of-valhalla (cooldown), pipes-of-the-sewers (charges), elemental-gem and feather-token bird/whip (quantity, single-use), and manual-of-golems (use, single-use). Separately, isStatefulMagicItemMechanics (packages/core/src/rules/magicItemMechanics.ts) marks every cooldownEconomy grant as stateful. That forces gem/token/manual stacks to quantity 1, although the pack prints them as stateless single-use consumables.

DESIGN (decided; do not substitute another):
1. BIND CREDIT. Add migration 0049 with a table `item_grant_bind_credit(credit_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, campaign_id, item_instance_id, pack_ref, variant_id NULL, economy_id, operation_id, issued_at, issued_elapsed_minutes NULL, redeemed_effect_id NULL, redeemed_at NULL, provenance, session_id)`. Follow the 0048 pattern: schema snapshot via `npm run schema:snapshot -w @eshyra/core`, plus the migration ledger expectations in migrationLegacyAdoption/persistence tests. credit_id is deterministic: `${item_instance_id}:${operation_id}:${n}`, with the smallest free n.
2. ISSUE. useItem (packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts) issues exactly ONE credit per completed use, inside its transaction, for each distinct economy E that satisfies all three conditions: (a) the operation's cost charged E by an amount > 0; (b) some grant in the row's EFFECTIVE mechanics (its variant) names cooldownEconomy E; (c) that grant is NOT grant-ended-anchored. Anchored grants keep their existing coupling unchanged. Exception: when this use destroys the instance, issue NO credit, because the existing consumption receipt already covers that case. Extend the result hint: today's hint.bindGrant names only anchored grants. Add `hint.bindCredits: [{creditId, economyId, grantIds}]` listing the grant ids that may redeem each credit. Update the use_item tool description to say so. Keep it concise.
3. REDEEM. validateItemGrantBinding / createActiveEffect (packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts) apply to a grant that names a NON-anchored cooldownEconomy E and is bound through a LIVE inventory row. Binding requires an unredeemed credit for the same campaign, instance and economy E. Redeem the OLDEST such credit (issued_at, then credit_id) atomically in the same transaction as the effect insert. If there is none, refuse with a message naming the operation that spends E ("use_item <operationId> first"). There is NO override. A DM who wants a creature outside the item's economy starts a ruling-sourced summoning instead; say this in the message. The consumed-instance receipt path stays as it is. Grants with no cooldownEconomy bind as today.
4. STACKS (xt6m, stacking part only). A grant whose cooldownEconomy names an economy of kind 'single-use' no longer, by itself, makes isStatefulMagicItemMechanics true. The other stateful triggers are unchanged. Stacks of gems, tokens and manuals can then be held and used one unit at a time: a surviving stack gets a credit (rule 2), and the last unit gets a receipt (the existing rule). Audit every caller that keyed off statefulness for these items: give_item allocation, use_item's quantity-1 guard, adoption split, and the stateful quantity guard in mutateState. Record them in your notes.
   Consequence for ids: give_item for a now-non-stateful gem uses the caller's explicit id. Today a retired explicit id is refused (the domainMutations `itemInstanceIdRetired` check in giveItem). Change that rule: an explicit id that is retired (and has no live row) is allocated `${id}#n`, with the smallest n for which itemInstanceIdTaken is false. The tool result's id reports the actual id (it already returns result.id). Make the result say clearly that the id was reassigned, for example `reassignedFrom`. Update the retired-id tests in packages/core/test/itemGrantConsumptionReceipt.test.ts accordingly: the explicit-retired give now succeeds under a fresh id, the original receipt is unchanged, and the raw-SQL trigger refusal stays.
5. NOT IN SCOPE: the readiness gate that refuses use_item break-gem/use-token on the unmodified pack (missing F3/F2/F5 hooks) belongs to eshyra-c58j. Keep using the readiness-waived pack in tests, following the existing precedent. The Efreeti hint text belongs to olc5.12.4. Control and obedience stay DM-adjudicated.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE (generalized over the real pack, readiness waived where required; no per-example sprawl):
- For EVERY non-anchored cooldownEconomy grant in the pack, enumerated from the pack itself rather than hard-coded: bind without a credit is refused; use_item followed by bind succeeds and redeems exactly one credit; a second bind is refused until another use. Drive the use step through each item's real spending operation. Where a carrier can't run use_item (readiness waived but another gate blocks it), record why in a test comment and in your notes, and exercise the credit table directly for that item only.
- Two uses then two binds succeed; a third bind is refused; the oldest credit redeems first.
- Credit scoping: wrong campaign, wrong instance, and wrong economy are refused. A refused effect insert leaves the credit unredeemed.
- Stacks: a 3-gem stack. Use, bind, use, bind each go through credits on the surviving row. The final use writes the receipt, its bind goes through the receipt, and attribution stays distinct in listActiveEffects.
- The anchored grants (Ring, Efreeti) are unchanged; their existing tests stay green.
VERIFY: run the focused suites first (itemGrantSummons, itemGrantConsumptionReceipt, itemState, activeEffects, persistence, migrationLegacyAdoption, domainMutations/give tests). Then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`; no pack change is expected, so if one appears, stop and report. Then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing.
If a decided point conflicts with code or source, record the precise conflict, leave the bead open, and stop.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-10-17 as a Claude Sonnet 5.5 Agent in .worktrees/eshyra-olc5.12.3.1 on branch eshyra-olc5.12.3.1, cut from eshyra-olc5.12.3 @ cccdda4f.
COMPLETE. Commit f53ec6457ae9c6db2b83fb3f0984d0eba661cb28 on branch eshyra-olc5.12.3.1 (not pushed, no PR, per dispatch).
CHANGES PER DESIGN POINT
1 Bind credit: migration 0049_item_grant_bind_credit.sql (table per plan + partial index on open credits), schema.snapshot regenerated, ledger expectations updated in migrationLegacyAdoption/persistence tests. itemGrantBinding.ts: issueItemGrantBindCredit (id <instance>:<operation>:<smallest free n>), oldestOpenItemGrantBindCredit, redeemItemGrantBindCredit.
2 Issue: useItem (itemState.ts issueBindCredits): one credit per distinct economy charged >0 that a non-anchored grant of the effective (variant) mechanics names; none when the use destroys the instance (instanceDestroyed tracked at both destroy sites; receipt covers it). hint now {bindGrant?, bindCredits?: [{creditId, economyId, grantIds}]}. use_item and start_effect tool descriptions updated.
3 Redeem: validateItemGrantBinding (activeEffects.ts) requires an open credit for non-anchored cooldownEconomy grants on a live row; refusal names the spending operation (use_item '<op>' first) and says to use a ruling-sourced summoning; no override. Redeemed in createActiveEffect right after the effect insert (same txn). Receipt path and anchored path unchanged.
4 Stacks: isStatefulMagicItemMechanics no longer counts a grant whose cooldownEconomy is a single-use economy. Gem/token/manual stacks are now stateless.
 Statefulness caller audit (all key off isStatefulMagicItem -> isStatefulMagicItemMechanics, so they change together): (a) toolGiveItem: stateful flag -> allocation base#n + item_state; now gem/token/manual use the caller's explicit id and no item_state; (b) useItem quantity-1 guard and stackedSingleUse path: stack of N uses one unit per call, last unit destroys + receipt (existing); (c) itemAdoption.adoptMagicItem split/stateful handling: same predicate, now treats these as stateless stacks (no code change); (d) mutateState stateful quantity guard keys on item_state row presence, so no row for these items -> stack quantity allowed (no code change); (e) giveItem stateful quantity-1 check (domainMutations) keys on the passed flag. No other callers.
 Retired ids: giveItem now reassigns a retired explicit id (no live row) to ${id}#n, smallest n with itemInstanceIdTaken false; result reports reassignedFrom (giveItem return and give_item tool data, plus a note). Stateful allocation unchanged.
CARRIERS (enumerated from the pack in itemGrantBindCredit.test.ts, 21 non-anchored cooldownEconomy grants across 12 items): bag-of-tricks, bowl/brazier/censer/stone elementals, deck-of-illusions (illusion grant), elemental-gem, feather-token bird-token and whip-token (object grant), figurine goat-of-traveling (9 variants), horn-of-valhalla, manual-of-golems, pipes-of-the-sewers. EVERY carrier was driven through its real spending operation via use_item (readiness waived for the carrier records, following existing precedent); none needed the credit table directly. Per carrier: bind without use refused; use -> hint.bindCredits; bind redeems exactly one; second bind refused; advance a week, use again, second bind succeeds. Stack carriers (gem, tokens, manual) held as stack of 3. Non-creature grants (deck card-illusion, whip-token) are refused by start_effect as DM-adjudicated before the credit is consulted; test asserts use_item still issues the credit listing the grant and the refused bind leaves it open.
TESTS: new packages/core/test/itemGrantBindCredit.test.ts (17 tests: pack enumeration, per-carrier lifecycle, two-uses/two-binds/third refused with oldest-first, wrong instance/campaign/economy refused and refused insert leaves credit open, refused use issues no credit, 3-gem stack use/bind/use/bind/last-use receipt/bind with attribution); new test/support/bindCredit.ts scaffold (grants the credit use_item would have issued) wired into itemGrantSummons.test.ts call() since those 21 existing tests exercise grant validation without the spend; itemGrantConsumptionReceipt.test.ts updated (retired explicit give now succeeds as <id>#1/#2 with reassignedFrom and original receipt unchanged; raw-SQL trigger refusal kept; stack-of-2 gem now usable, unused live gem refused); migrationLegacyAdoption/persistence ledger to 49.
VERIFY: npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack OK (no pack change). npm run verify:worktree exit 0: 366 test files passed | 2 skipped; 6969 tests passed | 3 skipped.
DEVIATION NOTES for review: (1) oldest credit ordering is issued_at then insertion rowid, not credit_id text, so n=10 sorts after n=9; (2) credits are also scoped by pack_ref and variant_id so a stale credit cannot be redeemed by a reused instance id; (3) credits are issued for non-creature grants too (deck, whip-token) per the literal rule; they are unredeemable (start_effect refuses those kinds) and could be filtered to creature grants in a follow-up; (4) outstanding credits are not cleaned up when a row is later destroyed/removed (inert).
Not touched: eshyra-olc5.12.3, eshyra-xt6m (left to dispatcher).
